THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Gafur Qureshi in a motor vehicle accident dated 31.12.2015.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the wife and children of deceased-Gafur Qureshi.
It is the case of the petitioners that on 31.12.2015 at about 10-30 a.m., deceased was returning from his sister's house.
He was proceedings towards Shashtri Nagar, Tashkhand of Sholapur city.

Near the Godown of Shivaji Beedi Factory, a Tempo bearing registration No.MH-12/5638 ('offending vehicle' for short), came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the accident, he sustained injuries and died on the spot.

As the owner and insurer respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5.
Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.
6. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.
As the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
Smt. Shameem And Ors vs M/S Sable Waghire Company Pvt. Ltd.

Exs.P1 to 9 are marked.

9. No witnesses are examined on behalf of respondent No.2, but copy of the insurance policy is marked as Ex.R.1.
10.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.9,00,000/- with interest at 9% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

11. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. awarded  1. Loss of income due to Rs.8,10,000/-
 dependency  2. Towards love and affection Rs.20,000/-
 3. Loss of estate Rs.20,000/-
 4. Towards loss of consortium Rs.30,000/-
 5. Towards transportation and Rs.20,000/-
 funeral expenses
12. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
13. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under other heads also requires enhancement and prays to allow the appeal.
14. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Heard arguments and perused the records.
16.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, Gafur Qureshi died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident has attained finality.
17. In the absence of proof of age of the deceased based on the post mortem report, the Tribunal has rightly taken the age of deceased as 40 years and 15 as the multiplier.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income of notional basis.

3 is of the year 2015, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m. instead of Rs.6,000/-
p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was in the age group of 40-50 years, 25% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1, (Magma's case).

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.10,000/-.
Since there are four dependents, 1/4th deducted towards his personal and living expenses is correct.

With these components, loss of dependency is Rs.10,000 x 12 x 15 x 3/4 =
13,50,000/-.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for (2018) 18 SCC 130 compensation of Rs.13,50,000/- as against Rs.8,10,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

18. As wife and children of the deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,60,000/- under the head loss of consortium as against Rs.30,000/-
granted by the Tribunal.
Separate compensation granted in a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

19. As per the National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma cases, when substantial compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, under the conventional heads, the petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses.

sentences.text: Hence, compensation under the head loss to estate and funeral (2017) 16 SCC 680 expenses (which includes transportation charges) is reduced to Rs.15,000/- each.

20. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.15,40,000/- as against Rs.9,00,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount Amount No. awarded by awarded by  the Tribunal this Court  1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,10,000/- Rs.13,50,000/-
 2. Towards love and Rs.20,000/- Disallowed  affection  3. Loss of estate Rs.20,000/- Rs.15,000/-

4 . Towards loss of Rs.30,000/- Rs.1,60,000/-
 consortium  5. Towards Rs.20,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 transportation and  funeral expenses  Rs.9,00,000/- Rs.15,40,000/-
21.

Since without any basis, the Tribunal has granted interest at 9% and in the light of decision in MFA No.103557/2016 dated 20.03.2018, the same is reduced to 6% and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a. Appeal is allowed in part. b.
Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.15,40,000/- together with interest at 6% per annum as Smt. Shameem And Ors vs M/S Sable Waghire Company Pvt. Ltd.
